source.publication: 2025 Expanded Instructions (IA 1040) and the 2025 IA 1040 Iowa Individual Income Tax Return
source.section: IA 1040 form PDF p.1 Step 3 lines a, b, d; form PDF p.2 lines 1c, 2-5, 7, 8, 11, 12; Instructions PDF p.8 Step 3; PDF p.9-10 lines 2-4; PDF p.12 line 5 ('Iowa now has a flat tax rate of 3.8%'); PDF p.18 line 12

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 35,500.00 = 35,500.00. Federal taxable income = 35,500.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 1 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older = 2,400.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IA 1040 filing status 2 (married filing jointly). Step 3 line a personal credits 2 x 40.00 = 80.00; line b 1 x 20.00 = 20.00 (65 or older on or before January 1, 2026; nobody blind); line c no dependents; line d and line 8 = 100.00. Line 1c federal AGI 35,500.00; line 2 federal taxable income 2,400.00. Schedule 1: no additions or subtractions. Schedule 1 line 21 net modifications = 0.00; line 3 = 0.00. Line 4 Iowa taxable income = 2,400.00 + (0.00) = 2,400.00. Line 5 tax = 3.8% x 2,400.00 = 91.20; line 7 = 91.20. Line 11 total credits 100.00; line 12 = 91.20 - 100.00, below zero, so enter 0.00 (non-refundable; expected credits shows the 91.20 used). State income tax 0.00 (no line 13-17 credits; line 19 school district or EMS surtax is local, not computed). The form allows whole-dollar rounding; expected keeps the cents. Low-income exemption and alternate tax (PDF p.10-13): line 4 2,400.00 + federal deduction 33,100.00 = 35,500.00, against 32,000.00: not exempt; alternate tax 4.3% x (35,500.00 - 32,000.00) = 150.50, not smaller than the 3.8% tax. The spouse is the one who is 65 or older: on a joint return the spouse's credit counts (PDF p.8). The tax of 91.20 is over the two personal credits of 80.00 and under 100.00, so the 65 credit decides the result.
accepted_approximations: School district and county EMS surtaxes (a percentage of the tax, form line 19) are local and out of scope (issue #1).
